hints: Start with each course's average: `GROUP BY dept, course_code`.
Compare each group against a subquery that averages its own department. The subquery needs to refer to the outer query's dept.
Compare the unrounded averages, and round only in the SELECT.
sampleDataSql:
INSERT INTO exam_results (result_id, dept, course_code, marks) VALUES
  (1, 'CSE', 'CS101', 80),
  (2, 'CSE', 'CS101', 90),
  (3, 'CSE', 'CS102', 60),
  (4, 'CSE', 'CS102', 70),
  (5, 'ME', 'ME201', 75),
  (6, 'ME', 'ME202', 75),
  (7, 'ME', 'ME202', 76);
statement:
Each row is one student's marks in one course. A course **stands out** when its average marks are strictly higher than the average of **all** marks in its department.

Return `dept`, `course_code` and `course_avg` (rounded to 2 decimal places) for every course that stands out, ordered by `dept`, then `course_code`.
title: Courses Above Their Department's Average
